The containment contracts for FormationAdjustment and Attacking under the search-task operation are satisfied by direct source-inventory containment under SearchRegion, so they are omitted. The three-state-area cardinality contract is bound to SearchRegion as owner with direct_child_states domain, left to the deterministic frontier via cardinality_bindings only.

cardinality_bindings.alternative_reading: An alternative reading could bind the owner to UAVSwarmStateMachine itself (counting SearchRegion and MissionRegion as two of three areas plus one more), but the source inventory shows only two named regions (SearchRegion, MissionRegion) under UAVSwarmStateMachine, which cannot satisfy 'three different state areas' as directly-owned regions; the four leaf states under SearchRegion is the only reading yielding a countable domain close to NL2's continuous search-task narrative, though NL2 could also be read as loosely referring to Idle/Searching/(FormationAdjustment+Attacking) as three thematic areas -- this remains a plausible competing reading for D review.
cardinality_bindings.basis: NL2 quote 'it operates within three different state areas'; exact_source_inventory.states rows for UAVSwarmStateMachine.SearchRegion.{Idle,Searching,FormationAdjustment,Attacking}; inspection_equivalent_facts.states SearchRegion children matching the same four leaf states; canonical_source_ir.model.concurrent_regions count=0 indicating no explicit region separator establishing concurrent_regions semantics.
cardinality_bindings.reason: NL2 explicitly counts 'three different state areas' as the direct operating substates of the UAV swarm's search-task operation. The exact source and closed-model inventories show UAVSwarmStateMachine.SearchRegion (author-source scope realizing the search-task operation) owning exactly the direct child states Idle, Searching, FormationAdjustment, and Attacking. However, per the contract-level owner rule, the counted owner scope is the search-task operation itself (UAVSwarmStateMachine/SearchRegion as its principal operating region), and the normative concept is direct child states/modes of that owner, not a concurrent-region partition -- NL2 states no parallel/orthogonal/simultaneously-active semantics, only a single continuous operating behavior moving among named areas. This is a behavior-consequence-relevant binding because the reachability defect above means none of these direct child states are actually reachable, which the deterministic frontier will need for its complete inventory comparison.

response.reason: The closed FCSTM shows the root machine llms_emp_feedback_final_0046 has an initial pseudostate edge (transition:line:40) that targets a synthetic UnspecifiedInitial leaf state with zero outgoing transitions, rather than entering UAVSwarmStateMachine. As a direct behavioral consequence, the entire UAVSwarmStateMachine composite (and its SearchRegion/MissionRegion children, all NL2/NL3/NL4 operating states) is unreachable from root, all six declared events have zero reachable consumers, and the machine is stuck in a deadlock leaf immediately after start. This lens grounds the downstream behavioral consequences of that structural defect: root reachability failure for the search-task operation, unreachable-consumer coverage for the Task_Assignment_Received event tied to NL4's transition contract, and the deterministic deadlock-frontier fact at UnspecifiedInitial. Existing endpoint/action/cardinality/containment contracts are left to the structural-contrast lens; this lens focuses on reachability, consumer coverage, and deadlock-frontier behavioral consequences, using inspection_equivalent_facts, verify_facts, and the fcstm_model text as deterministic evidence.

arguments.reason: Thirteen obligations were adjudicated. The dossier establishes a coherent picture: the closed FCSTM model has a root initial edge going only to a synthetic UnspecifiedInitial dead-end state, and neither UAVSwarmStateMachine nor any of its descendant states (SearchRegion, MissionRegion, Idle, Searching, FormationAdjustment, Attacking, MissionActive, MissionComplete) are reachable from that root, confirmed by verify_facts refuted reachability rows and inspection_equivalent_facts diagnostics (STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL, LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING, EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE). Distinct obligations properly separate: (a) owner-local initial-entry defects at UAVSwarmStateMachine scope (i0, i2), (b) global root-to-composite unreachability (i1, i5, i9 - i9 has an executed G1 backend receipt confirming verdict=false/unreachable), (c) event-consumer-coverage gaps for declared-but-unreachable consumers (i3, i6, i10), (d) a variable-delta/effect gap for the UAV-count-decrease requirement (i4), (e) a cardinality reading of SearchRegion's direct children showing 4 vs the NL's "three" (i8), (f) the well-formed-but-inert nested SearchRegion->Idle initial edge (i7), and (g) two containment obligations (i11, i12) whose deterministic frontier explicitly could not resolve owner/child identity to one exact closed-model state, leaving those two genuinely unresolved. Each decision below evaluates the exact supplied facts, checks for competent rebutting/undercutting readings per the strongest_rebuttal text, and applies the frontier discipline that a correct local edge or transition existence does not rebut an independent reachability, coverage, or effect defect at a different property/locus.

arguments.basis: Pair 0046 dossiers: fcstm_model, inspection_equivalent_facts, verify_facts, canonical_source_ir, and working_contract for the UAVSwarmStateMachine PlantUML/FCSTM model.

decisions.basis: fcstm_model.text lines 10/35, inspection_equivalent_facts diagnostics STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL, canonical_source_ir.model.initial_states.
decisions.reason: NL2 requires the swarm operation to actually enter its three state areas. The exact closed-model fact is that UAVSwarmStateMachine's own initial edge targets a synthetic zero-outgoing UnspecifiedInitial placeholder, never SearchRegion or MissionRegion (fcstm_model.text, STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL diagnostics). The authored nested SearchRegion edge is a separate owner scope and does not rebut this owner-local defect per the initial-entry scope protocol.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The well-formed nested SearchRegion-local edge '[*] -> Idle' shows author intent was correct, but this contract audits UAVSwarmStateMachine's own local edge, which is bound to a synthetic UnspecifiedInitial dead-end rather than SearchRegion/MissionRegion; a child region's internal edge cannot substitute for the owner's own edge, so the rebuttal is defeated by the exact owner-scope binding.
decisions.violated_obligation: UAVSwarmStateMachine (the UAV swarm search-task operation) must have an owner-local initial pseudostate edge entering one of its three authored state areas under SearchRegion/MissionRegion.

decisions.basis: verify_facts.checks reachability rows; inspection_equivalent_facts.reachable_state_refs; canonical_source_ir.model.initial_states.
decisions.reason: verify_facts.checks explicitly refutes reachability for state:UAVSwarmStateMachine:line:10 and state:SearchRegion:line:11 (reachable_from_initial=false), and inspection_equivalent_facts confirms only the root wrapper and one synthetic leaf are reachable. This is the same underlying defect confirmed with an executed backend receipt in obligation i9 for the same G1 predicate family.
decisions.strongest_defeater: One could argue the root '[*] -> UnspecifiedInitial' is only a compiler placeholder and canonical_source_ir shows the real intended entry, but verify_facts' deterministic reachability rows (status=refuted) are the exact fact this contract audits, and they show genuine unreachability in the tested closed model, defeating the placeholder-only reading.
decisions.violated_obligation: UAVSwarmStateMachine/SearchRegion composite must be reachable from the closed model's true root initial entry.

decisions.basis: event_consumer_fact rows for all six events; reachability_fact; verify_fact.
decisions.reason: The dossier's observed facts state all six required events have declared consumer transitions but empty reachable_consumer_transition_refs, i.e., none can execute from the model root given the same root-unreachability defect established elsewhere. A declared but unreachable consumer does not satisfy a reachable-consumer coverage contract per the property-preserving adjudication protocol.
decisions.strongest_defeater: Declaration-only consumer existence (the transitions exist with the correct triggers) could be argued as satisfying the contract, but reachable-consumer coverage is a distinct, stronger operational property from mere declared existence; the exact reachable_consumer_transition_refs are empty for all listed events, defeating the declaration-only reading.
decisions.violated_obligation: Required events (Start_Mission, Intercepted, Task_Assignment_Received, Formation_Adjusted, Attack_Completed_UAV_Count_Decreased, Mission_Completed) must have reachable consumers in the UAVSwarmStateMachine operating scope.

decisions.reason: The deterministic frontier explicitly retained this obligation as unresolved because the typed owner or child does not resolve to one exact closed-model state (binding_status=identity_unresolved, empty element_refs). The dossier genuinely cannot decide the exact containment claim without that binding, so this remains unresolved rather than established or not_established.
decisions.strongest_defeater: A later exact owner/carrier binding could close this check to one exact model identity; no identity is currently supplied to decide the containment claim one way or the other.
decisions.violated_obligation: The formation adjustment state must be one of the three state areas contained within the UAV swarm's search-task operation (containment check).

decisions.basis: fcstm_model.text nested UAVSwarmStateMachine block; inspection_equivalent_facts LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING and STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL diagnostics.
decisions.reason: fcstm_model.text shows UAVSwarmStateMachine's nested scope declares its own synthetic 'state UnspecifiedInitial' and '[*] -> UnspecifiedInitial;' instead of an edge to SearchRegion or MissionRegion, and that placeholder is a zero-outgoing leaf (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING diagnostic). This is exactly the malformed owner-local edge the initial-entry scope protocol treats as a source defect independent of any correct sibling/root edge.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The individually well-formed nested SearchRegion-local '[*] -> Idle' and MissionRegion-local '[*] -> MissionActive' edges might be read as satisfying entry semantics for those sub-scopes, but this contract's exact owner is UAVSwarmStateMachine itself, whose own edge targets a synthetic UnspecifiedInitial rather than SearchRegion/MissionRegion; a child region's edge cannot substitute for the parent's own malformed edge under the initial-entry scope protocol.

decisions.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers Task_Assignment_Received row; verify_facts.checks event-consumer refuted status.
decisions.reason: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers shows Task_Assignment_Received has consumer_transition_refs=[transition:line:19] but reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[] (empty), and verify_facts confirms event-consumer:Task_Assignment_Received status=refuted. Per the property-preserving adjudication protocol, a declared/correctly-targeted consumer does not rebut a reachable-consumer coverage violation.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The Searching->Attacking transition exists exactly as authored with the correct trigger, satisfying the transition-endpoint contract; but that is a weaker/different property from reachable-consumer coverage, which is the exact property this obligation audits, and reachable_consumer_transition_refs is empty, so the endpoint-existence rebuttal does not defeat this coverage violation.
decisions.violated_obligation: The Task_Assignment_Received event must be consumable (reachable) by the UAV swarm's in-flight/Searching operating scope so Searching->Attacking can fire.

decisions.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts transition row for transition:line:21; working_contract elements list.
decisions.reason: inspection_equivalent_facts shows transition:line:21 (Attacking->Searching, trigger Attack_Completed_UAV_Count_Decreased) has effects=[], and working_contract lists only R45RouteToken as a declared variable, which is compiler-owned and unrelated to UAV count. The exact carrier transition lacks the required effect, establishing the violation.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The event name itself textually encodes the intended decrease semantics, which might be argued as sufficient evidence of the effect; however, event naming is not an executable effect binding, and the frozen model's exact effects field on transition:line:21 is empty, with the only declared variable (R45RouteToken) being an unrelated compiler-owned route-control variable, defeating the naming-based rebuttal.
decisions.violated_obligation: The transition consuming Attack_Completed_UAV_Count_Decreased (Attacking->Searching) must carry an effect decreasing a UAV-count variable.

decisions.violated_obligation: The required operating scope UAVSwarmStateMachine must be reachable from the model root.

result.reason: Thirteen obligations were adjudicated. The dossier establishes a coherent picture: the closed FCSTM model has a root initial edge going only to a synthetic UnspecifiedInitial dead-end state, and neither UAVSwarmStateMachine nor any of its descendant states (SearchRegion, MissionRegion, Idle, Searching, FormationAdjustment, Attacking, MissionActive, MissionComplete) are reachable from that root, confirmed by verify_facts refuted reachability rows and inspection_equivalent_facts diagnostics (STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL, LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING, EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE). Distinct obligations properly separate: (a) owner-local initial-entry defects at UAVSwarmStateMachine scope (i0, i2), (b) global root-to-composite unreachability (i1, i5, i9 - i9 has an executed G1 backend receipt confirming verdict=false/unreachable), (c) event-consumer-coverage gaps for declared-but-unreachable consumers (i3, i6, i10), (d) a variable-delta/effect gap for the UAV-count-decrease requirement (i4), (e) a cardinality reading of SearchRegion's direct children showing 4 vs the NL's "three" (i8), (f) the well-formed-but-inert nested SearchRegion->Idle initial edge (i7), and (g) two containment obligations (i11, i12) whose deterministic frontier explicitly could not resolve owner/child identity to one exact closed-model state, leaving those two genuinely unresolved. Each decision below evaluates the exact supplied facts, checks for competent rebutting/undercutting readings per the strongest_rebuttal text, and applies the frontier discipline that a correct local edge or transition existence does not rebut an independent reachability, coverage, or effect defect at a different property/locus.

issues.basis: fcstm_model.text and inspection_equivalent_facts show two independent '[*] -> UnspecifiedInitial' edges (root scope and UAVSwarmStateMachine scope) with reachable_from_initial=true only for the outer UnspecifiedInitial; STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL diagnostics cover UAVSwarmStateMachine, SearchRegion, MissionRegion and all children; canonical_source_ir.model.initial_states records the intended SearchRegion.Idle/MissionRegion.MissionActive targets which are never reached from the owning UAVSwarmStateMachine scope in the closed model.
issues.expected: The UAV swarm search-task operation (UAVSwarmStateMachine) must have an owner-local initial pseudostate edge entering one of its three authored state areas (Idle/Searching/FormationAdjustment/Attacking under SearchRegion).
issues.observed: The closed FCSTM's only reachable initial chain is llms_emp_feedback_final_0046 -> UnspecifiedInitial (a zero-outgoing synthetic leaf). UAVSwarmStateMachine itself, and every state under SearchRegion/MissionRegion, are marked reachable_from_initial=false in inspection_equivalent_facts and refuted in verify_facts; the nested UAVSwarmStateMachine-local initial edge also targets a second synthetic UnspecifiedInitial rather than SearchRegion or MissionRegion.
issues.reason: NL2 requires the swarm's search-task operation to actually operate within its three state areas; the derived initial_entry contract's owner (UAV swarm search-task operation / UAVSwarmStateMachine) has no exact closed-model default entry reaching any of the three areas, only a synthetic zero-outgoing placeholder, so the obligation is unmet at the owner scope regardless of the well-formed nested SearchRegion-local edge.
issues.requirement_quote: it operates within three different state areas
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The authored PlantUML/canonical source shows a well-formed nested '[*] -> Idle' inside SearchRegion and '[*] -> MissionActive' inside MissionRegion, so author intent is well-formed; the defect is confined to the compiled FCSTM root/owner wiring, which is exactly the closed-model fact this contract audits, not a rebuttal to it.
issues.title: UAVSwarmStateMachine owner has no exact initial entry into SearchRegion's state areas; only a synthetic unspecified placeholder is reachable

issues.basis: verify_facts non_proved reachability rows for state:UAVSwarmStateMachine:line:10 and state:SearchRegion:line:11 (status=refuted); inspection_equivalent_facts metrics show unreachable_state_count=10 of 12 states and reachable_state_refs limited to the root wrapper and one synthetic leaf.
issues.expected: The composite realizing the UAV swarm's continuous pre-mission-completion search-task operation (UAVSwarmStateMachine/SearchRegion) must be reachable from the closed model's true root initial entry.
issues.observed: verify_facts.checks lists reachability:state:UAVSwarmStateMachine:line:10 and reachability:state:SearchRegion:line:11 both status=refuted with reachable_from_initial=false; inspection_equivalent_facts.reachable_state_refs contains only the root wrapper and the outer synthetic UnspecifiedInitial.
issues.reason: This is the global reachability gap distinct from the narrower owner-local initial_entry defect: even a corrected UAVSwarmStateMachine-local edge would not matter if the root itself never reaches UAVSwarmStateMachine, so both must be tracked as independent obligations per frontier discipline.
issues.requirement_quote: it operates within three different state areas
issues.strongest_rebuttal: One could argue the root-level '[*] -> UnspecifiedInitial' is only a compiler-generated placeholder and the real author intent (SearchRegion.Idle as first state) is captured in canonical_source_ir.model.initial_states, but the deterministic closed-model reachability facts are what this contract audits, and they show the composite is genuinely unreachable in the tested FCSTM.
issues.title: UAVSwarmStateMachine and SearchRegion are unreachable from the closed-model root initial entry

issues.basis: fcstm_model.text nested block under UAVSwarmStateMachine defines synthetic UnspecifiedInitial and its own [*] edge; inspection_equivalent_facts diagnostic LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING refs state:UnspecifiedInitial:line:9 (root) and STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL covers state:UnspecifiedInitial:line:35 (nested) as well as SearchRegion/MissionRegion.
issues.expected: UAVSwarmStateMachine's local default-entry initial pseudostate edge should enter SearchRegion (or MissionRegion), the authored operating regions realizing the swarm's state areas.
issues.observed: fcstm_model.text shows UAVSwarmStateMachine's nested scope declares its own synthetic 'state UnspecifiedInitial' and '[*] -> UnspecifiedInitial;' rather than any edge to SearchRegion or MissionRegion; that placeholder has zero outgoing transitions (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING diagnostic).
issues.reason: Per the strict owner rule, an initial edge owned by a nested region cannot satisfy an entry contract owned by the parent composite; UAVSwarmStateMachine's own edge is authored to a synthetic dead-end rather than to SearchRegion/MissionRegion, so this is a distinct malformed owner-local edge obligation.
issues.requirement_quote: it operates within three different state areas
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The nested SearchRegion-local edge '[*] -> Idle' and MissionRegion-local edge '[*] -> MissionActive' are individually well-formed, which could be read as satisfying entry semantics for those sub-scopes; but this contract's owner is UAVSwarmStateMachine itself, whose own local pseudostate edge is what is malformed, and a child region's internal edge cannot substitute for its owner's edge.
issues.title: UAVSwarmStateMachine's own local initial edge targets a synthetic placeholder instead of SearchRegion/MissionRegion

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers row for event Task_Assignment_Received (declared_ref event:Task_Assignment_Received:line:5, consumer_transition_refs=[transition:line:19], reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]); verify_facts.checks non_proved event-consumer:Task_Assignment_Received status=refuted.
issues.expected: The Task_Assignment_Received event must be consumable (reachable) by the UAV swarm's in-flight/Searching operating scope so the Searching->Attacking transition can actually fire.
issues.observed: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers for Task_Assignment_Received lists consumer_transition_refs=[transition:line:19] but reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[] (empty); verify_facts confirms event-consumer:Task_Assignment_Received status=refuted; diagnostic EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE explicitly names this event.
issues.reason: This is the independent operational-coverage property distinguished from the endpoint contract: a declared, correctly-targeted consumer transition is not the same as a reachable consumer, and the deterministic facts show zero reachable consumers for this exact event in its required scope.
issues.requirement_quote: During flight, if task assignment information is received, it enters the attack state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The Searching->Attacking transition (transition:line:19) exists exactly as authored with the correct trigger, so the transition-endpoint contract itself is satisfied; the unreachability stems entirely from the upstream initial-entry/root-reachability gap in UAVSwarmStateMachine, not from any defect in the transition's own definition.
issues.title: Task_Assignment_Received event has a declared consumer transition but no reachable consumer under the current initial-entry topology

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions row transition_ref=transition:line:21 (source Attacking, target Searching, triggers=[Attack_Completed_UAV_Count_Decreased], effects=[]); working_contract elements list only R45RouteToken as a declared route_control_variable, compiler-owned and unrelated to UAV count.
issues.expected: The transition consuming Attack_Completed_UAV_Count_Decreased (exiting the attack state) must carry an effect that decreases a variable representing the number of UAVs in the swarm.
locus_names: number of UAVs in the swarm
issues.observed: inspection_equivalent_facts transition at transition:line:21 (Attacking -> Searching, trigger Attack_Completed_UAV_Count_Decreased) has effects=[]; the closed model's only declared variable is R45RouteToken, an internal compiler-owned route-control variable (working_contract element compiler:route_control:R45RouteToken), not a UAV-count variable.
issues.reason: No frozen predicate expresses a transition-effect/variable-delta claim, so per routing discipline this remains a predicate-null W1 candidate bound to the exact carrier transition that lacks the required effect.
issues.requirement_quote: After completing the attack, the number of UAVs in the swarm decreases accordingly.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The event name itself ('Attack Completed / UAV Count Decreased') textually encodes the intended semantics, which could be argued as sufficient evidence of the effect; however, event naming is not an executable effect binding, and the frozen registry requires an actual effect field on the carrier transition, which is empty.
issues.title: Attacking->Searching transition (Attack_Completed_UAV_Count_Decreased) has no bound effect decreasing any UAV-count variable

issues.basis: fcstm_model.text lines 9-10,35,40; inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL (state:UAVSwarmStateMachine:line:10 and descendants); verify_facts.checks reachability:state:UAVSwarmStateMachine:line:10 status=refuted.
issues.expected: The root of the closed FCSTM must reach UAVSwarmStateMachine so the continuous search-task operating behavior across its three state areas can occur.
issues.observed: The only top-level initial edge (transition:line:40) targets a synthetic UnspecifiedInitial leaf state with zero outgoing transitions instead of UAVSwarmStateMachine; deterministic facts mark UAVSwarmStateMachine, SearchRegion, MissionRegion, and every leaf state beneath them as reachable_from_initial=false, and verify_facts refutes reachability for state:UAVSwarmStateMachine:line:10.
issues.reason: This is the clearest behavioral consequence in the model: a single misrouted root initial edge makes the entire search-task operation, and therefore the whole NL2 continuous-behavior obligation, dead on arrival. G1 (finite reachability) is the correct minimal frozen predicate for this exact source/target pair.
issues.requirement_quote: Before the mission is completed, the UAV swarm continuously performs target search tasks, during which it operates within three different state areas.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The nested UAVSwarmStateMachine.UnspecifiedInitial and UAVSwarmStateMachine's own internal [*] -> UnspecifiedInitial edge are separate obligations; one could argue the search-task operation is 'present' in the model even if unreachable, but presence without reachability cannot satisfy a continuous-operation obligation.
issues.title: UAVSwarmStateMachine (and all three NL2 state areas) unreachable from root initial entry

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers (Task_Assignment_Received row); inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE; verify_facts.checks event-consumer:Task_Assignment_Received status=refuted.
issues.expected: At least one consumer transition for Task_Assignment_Received must be reachable from the machine's root so the NL4 attack-entry response can actually occur during flight.
issues.observed: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers shows Task_Assignment_Received's declared consumer_transition_refs=[transition:line:19] but reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[] (empty); EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE diagnostic and verify_facts event-consumer check both confirm zero reachable consumption, caused by Searching itself being unreachable from root.
issues.reason: This candidate isolates the reachable-consumer-coverage consequence, distinct from the wrong-target/reachability contracts, per the frontier discipline requiring one candidate per distinct property with supporting facts aggregated in basis.
issues.requirement_quote: During flight, if task assignment information is received, it enters the attack state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The transition Searching -> Attacking (line 19) exists structurally and is correctly triggered/targeted, so one could argue the endpoint contract (NL-CONTRACT-REF-004) alone captures the defect; however, event_consumer_coverage is an independent operational property (whether the event can ever actually be consumed), not just endpoint existence, so a separate coverage candidate is warranted per the routing discipline.
issues.title: Task_Assignment_Received has a declared consumer transition but zero reachable consumers

issues.basis: fcstm_model.text line 16 ([*] -> Idle within SearchRegion); inspection_equivalent_facts.states SearchRegion/Idle reachable_from_initial=false; verify_facts.checks reachability:state:SearchRegion:line:11 and reachability:state:Idle:line:12 status=refuted.
issues.expected: The UAV swarm's search-task operation must have a functioning owner-local initial entry into one of its three state areas (Idle) that actually executes as part of reaching the search-task operation.
issues.observed: SearchRegion's internal initial edge [*] -> Idle (transition:line:16) exists and targets the correct state, but because UAVSwarmStateMachine and SearchRegion are themselves unreachable from the machine root (STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL diagnostics on SearchRegion:line:11 and Idle:line:12; verify_facts refutes reachability for both), this local initial edge is never operationally exercised.
issues.reason: Included as W1 candidate because although the edge exists (favoring satisfaction), the frontier discipline notes owner default entry and root reachability are independent properties that must both be tracked; however since the edge itself is well-formed and correctly targeted, this is preserved here only as a cautious candidate rather than omitted, flagging the operational inertness caused by the upstream defect for downstream adjudication.
issues.requirement_quote: it operates within three different state areas
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The local initial edge SearchRegion -> Idle is itself well-formed and syntactically satisfies the owner-local initial_entry obligation in isolation; per frontier discipline a satisfied local entry edge should not be turned into a downstream deadlock/reachability issue, so this observation may be better captured entirely by the separate root-reachability candidate above rather than as an independent initial_entry defect.
issues.title: Owner-local initial entry into SearchRegion.Idle is structurally present but operationally inert due to unreachable owner

branches.reason: This lens grounds NL contracts against the source inventory and closed FCSTM structure for case 0046 (UAV swarm). The closed model duplicates the intended SearchRegion/MissionRegion topology under a synthetic root wrapper with two independent [*]->UnspecifiedInitial edges (at machine-root level and inside UAVSwarmStateMachine), while UAVSwarmStateMachine itself and all of SearchRegion/MissionRegion/their children are unreachable from the root initial entry per inspection_equivalent_facts, verify_facts, and diagnostics. This breaks the owner-local initial_entry contract for the search-task operation, cascades to unreachable containment targets (FormationAdjustment, Attacking) that nonetheless keep their exact modeled endpoints, and leaves every declared event consumer (Intercepted, Task_Assignment_Received, Mission_Completed, etc.) structurally unreachable, directly matching the derived event_consumer_coverage contract. The endpoint transitions themselves (Searching->FormationAdjustment on Intercepted; Searching->Attacking on Task_Assignment_Received) exist with correct source/target/trigger in the closed model, so those two exact ENDPOINT contracts are satisfied and omitted.
